report.summary: Reviewed the supplied time-policy sources statically, with no tools other than the required skill load and no execution. The strict matcher does now gate setup: both write and readback records must carry the session UUID, case-derived marker, localStart, exactly one resolvable instant equal to instant[0], and the expected status, and the cancel POST URL is built only from the UUID-validated setup record. That claim holds. The final-replay claim also holds: every terminal runner return goes through evaluateTimeTrace, so no loose-result path exists. The per-run native row cap matches the budgets (v1 18, v2 24). However, cancellation-baseline failures are treated as terminal rather than per-case: once one cancel case cannot be established, every remaining case's expected requests are still taken from the trace, so the real cancel probe is never sent and the rest of the run is dropped as unknown. The added tests in tests/time-policy.test.ts (lines 114-117) use a v1 plan with v2-sized traces and trace-length assertions (25 rows/12 POSTs), which a 12-case v1 plan cannot produce; the bug they claim to cover is therefore not actually exercised by the code that handles the problem. Neither issue changes the native server's authorization, but both break the dependent-write probe's product value and its evidence. v1 frozen-case byte equality cannot be verified from the packet because fixtures/time-policy-v1-frozen.json is not supplied.

findings.title: A failed cancellation setup ends the whole run instead of only that case, so later cancel probes never send
findings.evidence: When setup or baseline does not match, the runner pushes an outcome 'unknown' with reason cancellation_setup_not_established and then does `continue` (lines 39-43). It does not tell evaluateTimeTrace about this. evaluateTimeTrace (lib/time-policy.ts:108-120) walks through every case in order and uses `take()` to consume the exact frozen request sequence; any extra or missing row throws DomainError 'Time trace request differs...' (503). The loop order, as generated by timePolicyCases (time-policy.ts:76), is cancel_below, cancel_exact, cancel_above, which are consecutive cases. So after the first failed setup, the runner still sends the setup POST and GET for the next cancel case. That trace has requests where the replay expects the real cancel POST `bookings/${id}/cancel` and its readback. On the first cancel case that does succeed, the runner never sends the `/cancel` POST. After the loop, line 45 calls evaluateTimeTrace, which throws, and line 46 catches the error and returns results=[results, ...].map unknown with reason 'authorization_or_state_changed'. As a result: (a) the trace omits a cancel POST, so the cancellation_deadline and preservation checks are never tested for any cancel case; (b) results that were already observed (for example, the create cases) are replaced with unknown; (c) the stored reason no longer names the real cause (setup_not_established) and says authorization_or_state_changed instead. The test at tests/time-policy.test.ts:115 expects trace.length===25 and 12 POSTs, but a v1 DEFAULT_TIME_PLAN has 12 cases (8 create + 3 cancel + 1 dst), whose full trace is 31 rows with 13 POSTs and stops at 2 POSTs after a per-case abort. Those exact numbers would describe a 17-case v2/cancel-credit run, not this one. Static count: metadata GET 1 + create 8×2 = 16 + cancel case1 setup 2 = 19, giving at most 19 rows and 10 POSTs. The assertion is therefore false for this flow, so the new regression does not really cover the intended per-case semantics.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted reasoning trace. Use session() = v1 DEFAULT_TIME_PLAN (12 cases, as in tests/time-policy.test.ts:115). Wrap the native handler so that it returns body.id='----...' (or a mismatching instant) for every active record. The runner sends metadata. create cases 0-7 match and are observed. Case cancel_below: setup POST and baseline GET come back mismatched, and the result is unknown/cancellation_setup_not_established. cancel_exact: the setup POST and GET are sent (trace rows 19-20). The loop then ends, because cancel_above still sends its setup pair? No: trace rows 21-22 are sent for the next iteration before any replay failure. All 11 sends have happened only if there are three cancel cases. At line 45 the replay reads row 21 expecting POST bookings/<id>/cancel and throws. The catch at line 46 returns every case, including the eight observed creates, as unknown with reason authorization_or_state_changed, and the trace has no /cancel POST at all. Suggested check (not executed): assert that the trace contains a /cancel row after a second successful setup, and that created-case results are preserved.
findings.suggestion: Keep the per-case 'continue' consistent with the replay contract. Either (A) add a frozen per-case 'skipped' marker to the trace and teach evaluateTimeTrace to consume it, or (B) make a cancellation setup failure a terminal incomplete stop, for example by throwing/new Incomplete('cancellation_setup_not_established') so the replay stops at the same row and only the remaining cases become unknown while earlier results are preserved. Then correct tests/time-policy.test.ts:115 to the actual row and POST counts (19 rows / 10 POSTs for v1, with zero /cancel rows), and assert that earlier observed results survive.

findings.title: The forged-record regression test asserts trace sizes that its own v1 plan cannot produce, and never proves a cancel POST was withheld
findings.evidence: The test builds `s=session()` (v1 DEFAULT_TIME_PLAN, 12 cases) and expects trace.length===25 and 12 POSTs. The budget and case math (8 create ×2 + 3 cancel ×4 + 1 dst ×2 + 1 meta = 31 rows, 13 POSTs, as asserted at line 46) means 25 rows/12 POSTs can only come from a 17-case v2/calendar or cancel-credit scenario with incomplete cancel cases. In addition, the assertion asserts that the trace has no /cancel row, which is exactly the omission that leaves the dependent-cancel check untested (see the P2 finding). The test also asserts `output.results.some(r=>r.outcome==='mismatch')`. That depends only on the tampered create readbacks, not on the strict UUID/instant gate. A forgery applied only to records whose case_id ends in -setup would still be 'covered' without exercising the setup-to-cancel linkage, and the middleware rewrites the body of every active record, so it cannot tell whether a cancel POST was legitimately blocked or silently skipped.
findings.reproduction: Static count for the fixture used at line 115: 12 cases → expected trace 31 (13 POSTs). Strict gate failure on the first cancel case yields at most 19 rows (10 POSTs), with no /cancel row and zero observed results after replay error. The asserted 25/12 values are unreachable for this input. Label: unexecuted; derived from lib/time-policy.ts:73-85, lib/time-policy-runner.ts:16-46.
findings.suggestion: Use a v1 trace-length assertion that matches the actual per-case flow, for example 19 rows / 10 POSTs / 0 /cancel rows. Restrict tampering to records whose caseId ends with '-setup' (or the caseId for each cancel case), and assert explicitly that no path ending in '/cancel' was requested while a control run without tampering does request three /cancel rows.

limitations: Static inline-source review only; no code was executed and no test, typecheck, build, or live/staging check was run.

lib/project-journey.ts, lib/domain.ts, tests/fixtures/time-policy-v1-frozen.json, tests/fixtures/seller-staging-hosted/0007_time_policy.sql, drizzle/0008_time_policy_sessions.sql, and the caller that persists runner output are not in the packet, so the byte-for-byte v1 frozen-case equality claim, registration validation, migration/row-limit schema, and the UI/result-display path cannot be verified.

The severity of the P2 depends on the runner's caller treating a thrown DomainError from executeTimePolicy's outer try as caught and replay-failed by line 46, which the packet shows, and on no caller-side suppression, which was not inspected.
The P2 trace counts (19 rows/10 POSTs after the first cancel case) are hand-counted from timePolicyCases ordering; they were not confirmed by execution.

The v2 calendar semantics (overnight interval, closed-date spill, frozen v1 cases) were checked only by reading the oracle, runner, and native worker against each other. Their agreement was not confirmed by running any test.

The native row cap (v1=18, v2=24 at time-policy-service.mjs:52) agrees with timePolicyBudget at lib/time-policy.ts:20. If production row scoping, the purge clause, or global-cap behavior differs beyond the supplied worker, that was not assessed.
